item.title: Charles Barkley Takes Swipe at Aaron Rodgers as He Plans TV Exit
item.description: Charles Barkley and Aaron Rodgers - Charles Barkley and Aaron Rodgers (Mitchell Layton and Logan Bowles/Getty Images Charles Barkley is making one thing clear as he embarks on what he insists will be his final year on TV: he won’t be following Aaron Rodgers ‘ playbook on his way out. During a recent appearance on Adam Schein’s Mad Dog Sports Radio show to kick off the 2026–27 NBA season, the 63-year-old Inside the NBA analyst was asked about his ongoing retirement claims. When Schein compared his current media run to Rodgers’ NFL farewell tour, Barkley drew a firm line between himself and the 42-year-old quarterback. “I’m not gonna bury everybody going out the door like Aaron,” Barkley said on the episode. “I’m not gonna burn every bridge and talk bad about all my exes on my way out the door like he’s doing.” You asked for it! You got it! Hall of Famer, Inside the NBA star, my guy Charles Barkley live on #ScheinOnSports now! @MadDogRadio — Adam Schein (@AdamSchein) October 21, 2026 Barkley’s remark referenced Rodgers’ recent appearance on Cam Heyward ‘s Not Just Football podcast, where the quarterback made headlines by calling out former partners Shailene Woodley and Danica Patrick along with former Green Bay Packers teammates Greg Jennings and Jermichael Finley. This isn’t the first time he has taken aim at the NFL star. Back in January 2024, Barkley bluntly declared during a CBS Mornings segment that he would have “ punched Aaron Rodgers in the face ” after the quarterback implied Jimmy Kimmel was associated with Jeffrey Epstein. Related Mike McCarthy Regrets Cursing at Aaron Rodgers in Viral Hot Mic Exchange While Barkley joked he won’t be taking shots at personal exes, the outspoken analyst has never shied away from criticizing corporate higher-ups. Ever since TNT Sports lost its NBA broadcast rights, Barkley has openly aired his grievances against the network executives. Sports fans and media insiders alike have pointed out a distinction between the two farewell tours: while Rodgers’ retirement is expected to be his final ride, few actually believe Barkley is hanging it up for good. On social media, fans have reacted to the potential end of Barkley’s broadcast era, with some even speculating on who could fill his shoes. One user on X shared a post that said: “I can’t even think about Barkley being gone. It really, really bums me out. He’s such a lovable doofus and Blake [Griffin] def doesn’t have that vibe. (IMO!)” Underneath that post, another user commented : “Charles has said this year is his last like 5 years in a row now so who knows if he really will.” While Barkley has teased retirement for years, he has returned for lucrative broadcasting deals and his latest exit tour comes with skepticism from viewers wondering if he will find a way back to the mic. The 2-2 draw maintained a unbeaten run for Derek McInnes' side but brought an end to a sequence of seven straight wins. item.title: Brewers make exciting, but risky, Brandon Woodruff World Series roster decision
item.description: Brewers make exciting, but risky, Brandon Woodruff World Series roster decision originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers are facing off against the Tampa Bay Rays in the 2026 MLB World Series. It's sure to be a great series, and it begins Friday night in Milwaukee. But before they could begin, the Brewers had a big decision to make with their World Series roster. When the Brewers announced their roster Friday morning, it featured a very notable name: Brandon Woodruff. Woodruff's inclusion on the roster is a very exciting decision for Brewers fans, as the beloved right-hander is back from injury and might actually play a real role in this World Series. But his inclusion comes with a big risk. Brewers make exciting and risky Brandon Woodruff decision on World Series roster Woodruff was initially feared to have suffered a season-ending shoulder injury earlier this season. He was placed on the injured list and missed the rest of the regular season. The two-time All-Star, who had a 2.98 ERA across nine starts with 47 strikeouts in 45.1 innings of work, missed the bulk of the 2026 MLB season. But now, with the Brewers making the World Series, he's back on the roster and is easily one of the more exciting storylines to follow at this year's World Series. Brewers fans should be excited to see Woodruff on the roster, but they should also be well aware of the risk that comes with such a decision. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player If Woodruff were to get hurt during the World Series and be forced to miss any time, the Brewers wouldn't be able to make a roster substitution based on the current understanding of MLB rules. As The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal reported, "The Brewers' fear with Woodruff, according to club officials briefed on his situation, is that any injury he suffers might be viewed as recurring or pre-existing, making the team unable to add another pitcher in his place." This decision from the Brewers was made even after knowing the risks, so they either feel confident that they'll be able to get a substitution, or that Woodruff is good enough to go and make a real impact on the team in the World Series. It will be a storyline worth following along with closely during the World Series, as seeing how he's utilized and whether this risk comes into play or not could have a big impact on the outcome of this series. item.title: Anthony Richardson marijuana charges, explained: Why Colts QB was cited for posession during traffic stop
item.description: Anthony Richardson marijuana charges, explained: Why Colts QB was cited for posession during traffic stop originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A sordid 2026 campaign for the Colts grew all the more disappointing on Friday after news broke that backup quarterback Anthony Richardson was charged with possession of marijuana after being forced to pull over earlier in Oct. Richardson, 24, is the latest of Indianapolis players to face the thorn-like teeth of the legal system. His charge proved far less benign than Keenan Allen, who was suspended three games after being jailed on drunk driving charges. Nevertheless, the incident adds more pressure to an already fractious situation within Indianapolis' ranks. Here's what you need to know. MORE: What Chris Ballard firing means for Shane Steichen's immediate future with Colts Anthony Richardson marijuana charges Richardson was the subject of a traffic stop on Oct. 12. Police stopped him as he drove a black 2023 Dodge Charger through Carmel, a suburban town located nearby Lucas Oil Stadium. According to court documents obtained by Fox 59 and CBS 4 , officers smelled the "odor of marijuana" while approaching Richardson's vehicle. The Colts quarterback reportedly admitted that he smokes marijuana inside the vehicle to avoid smoking in front of his children. He also revealed that he had a small amount of marijuana in the vehicle. MORE: Why Colts fans are calling for Daniel Jones benching Police placed Richardson in handcuffs before examining his vehicle. During the search, officers found a Mason jar containing what looked to be marijuana as well as an opened bag of THC-infused gummies. The substances tested positive for THC, according to court documents. Richardson was summarily handed a citation — the plates on his vehicle reportedly did not match its registration and was expired. He was also charged with a Class B misdemeanor charge for possession of marijuana. The charge was officially filed on Oct. 19. Per Fox 59, Richardson has his initial hearing waived. He is expected to arrive in court on Jan. 4, 2027, per court records examined by Fox 59. Colts react to Anthony Richardson marijuana incident Indianapolis released the following statement after Richardson was charged with possession of marijuana. "We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information," the statement read. "We will have no further comment at this time." item.title: AFC Wimbledon's Skiverton diagnosed with cancer
item.description: Terry Skiverton joined AFC Wimbledon in May 2022 as assistant to Johnnie Jackson [Getty Images] AFC Wimbledon assistant manager Terry Skiverton has been diagnosed with throat cancer and is scheduled to begin treatment in the coming weeks. The League One club said Skiverton had faced further health challenges since announcing in July that he would take time away from his duties to recover from ankle surgery. A club statement said: "Terry has been receiving valuable support from the League Managers Association (LMA) in recent months, and the club will continue to stand alongside him and his family throughout his treatment and recovery. "Everyone at AFC Wimbledon sends Terry their heartfelt best wishes as he prepares for the next stage of his treatment." item.title: Ravenna confirm date for Ronaldinho’s return to the pitch: ‘It’s real’
item.description: Ravenna confirm date for Ronaldinho’s return to the pitch: ‘It’s real’ Ravenna President Ignazio Cipriani confirms Brazilian legend Ronaldinho will take part in a Serie C match against Forlì on November 15: ‘The return is real.’ Former Milan and Barcelona star Ronaldinho will return to the pitch for a competitive match on November 15, 2026. The former Brazil international will feature in a derby between Ravenna and Forlì in Italy’s Serie C, the country’s third division. Official: Ronaldinho’s return date revealed PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – JUNE 19: Ronaldinho attends the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group C match between Brazil and Haiti at Philadelphia Stadium on June 19, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) “The Magic never left; now it’s time to bring him back onto the pitch. The return is real,” Ravenna President Ignazio Cipriani said in a statement via Ansa. “They told us it was impossible. On November 15, Ronaldinho will take the pitch at Stadio Benelli in our shirt, and in a match as important as the derby against Forlì. “We believed in it from day one and, thanks to the passion and work of our whole team, we turned an idea that seemed impossible into an occasion the entire world now awaits.” EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – JULY 19: Ronaldinho, Madonna and Ronaldo perform during the Topps Final Halftime Show in the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Ravenna confirmed Ronaldinho’s signing at an event in Miami this past June. The former Brazilian star hasn’t yet trained with the team, but, as Corriere della Sera reported, he has been watching their games, and his brother and agent, Roberto De Assis, was spotted at Ravenna’s stadium at the end of September. It’s still unclear how many minutes Ronaldinho will play, but his return to action has now been confirmed. The 46-year-old last played a competitive match over 10 years ago, with Fluminense in 2015.

item.title: Arsenal consult specialists over Saka injury
item.description: Arsenal consult specialists over Saka injury Mikel Arteta has admitted there are worrying signs around Bukayo Saka’s injury, with Arsenal still waiting for further scans before they know how serious the problem is. Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images Mikel Arteta has given a worrying update on Bukayo Saka , with the Arsenal winger needing more scans and specialist opinions before the club can say exactly what the problem is or how long he might be out. Saka lasted only 10 minutes of Arsenal’s Champions League draw away to Bayern Munich , and Arteta’s immediate assessment after the game was hardly encouraging . His latest update, given at his press conference before Saturday’s match against Everton , has not brought much reassurance. Arteta said : “He’s got another MRI this afternoon because he had a lot of fluid. “We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. Let’s be a little bit patient so we can give a definitive answer. Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images “We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialist. Obviously when a player has to walk off the pitch, he’s struggling to walk without any pain, he’s restricted to movement, they are not good signs. “So again, let’s be a little bit patient so we can give a definitive assessment and then let you know.” Saka was struggling to walk without pain after coming off in Munich and Arteta himself described that as “not good signs”. He was also spotted using crutches. item.description: It is only eight months since Bruno Fernandes was reflecting on the impact Michael Carrick had made and how he had predicted it. Carrick was part of some of United’s greatest European nights even if, in his understated way, it was rarely all about him. He was in charge for one of the worst, Wednesday’s 4-1 walloping at Como , again insisting it was not about him. item.title: Chesterfield's Grigg joins Forest Green Rovers
item.description: Will Grigg scored 25 goals in all competitions in his first season at Chesterfield, helping the club win the National League title in 2023-24 [Getty Images] Forest Green Rovers have signed experienced striker Will Grigg on a free transfer from Chesterfield on a deal until June 2028. The 35-year-old has scored 192 career goals and made more than 500 appearances in the English Football League during spells with Walsall, Brentford, MK Dons, Wigan Athletic, Sunderland, Rotherham United and Chesterfield. Grigg, who came close to joining Shrewsbury Town in August, could make his Forest Green debut in Saturday's National League game at Barrow. The Northern Ireland international spent three years at Chesterfield, scoring 42 goals in 118 appearances. He helped the Spireites win the National League title in 2024, securing their return to the EFL after six years outside England's top four divisions. "It is a special club with incredible people working hard every day to be successful," Grigg told Chesterfield's club website. "It was a big decision for me personally to drop down when I first joined the club and I haven't regretted that decision for one second."

item.title: Goodell says NFL's France debut 'just the beginning'
item.description: National Football League commissioner Roger Goodell is pictured ahead of the first NFL regular season game to be played in France (Joel Saget) NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said he believes the sport has a long-term future in France ahead of Sunday's first regular-season game in the country. The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will face off in Paris this weekend as the league continues its international expansion, despite authorities bracing for further demonstrations following riots and street violence across France last weekend. A record nine NFL games will be played outside the United States this year, with Paris joining Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro as new host cities. Goodell said the French capital was central to the league's long-term plans and suggested Sunday's game would be the first of many. "We're not announcing anything because we always like to get through the first one and the second one before we do. We are not coming here as a one-off," Goodell told AFP on Friday. "This is part of our efforts long-term to be successful. We're going to be here and be part of the culture. This is just the beginning." The NFL is seeking to build on the growing popularity of American sports in France, where the NBA has staged several regular-season games in recent years. Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs played a pair of games against the Indiana Pacers in Paris last year and are scheduled to return in January 2027. Goodell said France's sporting culture and Paris's global appeal made it an attractive market for the NFL. "We have a very strong fan base here that is growing and we want to see it accelerate and continue to grow. The iconic nature of this city is amazing," he said. "It is one of the international cities that if you're going to be global, you want to play in and you want to be a part of. We don't want to just play here. We want to be part of the culture. "We believe we should be a global sport. We think we can. Relationships with cities like Paris and markets like France are really important ultimately to our growth," he added. Goodell ultimately hopes the NFL will have as many as 16 international games per season with each team playing abroad every year. "We have ambitions to play 16 games (outside the US). We look at it -- more than (one game) per week -- it's really having every team participate in an international game in a given year," he said. "And since we have 32 teams, that works out pretty well having 16 games. And I think that's ultimately what we're focused on. We're at nine now. We're looking at expanding even beyond that." Goodell even suggested a Super Bowl could one day be staged outside the US if the league were to establish a franchise overseas. "Is it possible someday there'll be an NFL franchise in Paris? Yes, I do. I do think that's possible. And if that is possible, potentially a Super Bowl is possible too," he said. nip-mw/gj

item.title: Cole Kmet injury update: Where the Bears stand after tight end's exit
item.description: Cole Kmet injury update: Where the Bears stand after tight end's exit originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears pulled off a win over the New England Patriots during Thursday Night Football, 30-24, but it wasn't all smiles. During the game, they lost one of their strongest players when tight end Cole Kmet exited the game late due to a knee injury. With the Bears nearing the end of their second-to-last possession, Kmet went down with a knee injury after picking up 8 yards on a pass midway through the fourth quarter. He was later carted to the locker room, offering a thumbs-up to fans at Soldier Field along the way. While the gesture offered a small reason for optimism, his immediate removal from the game was troubling news for Chicago, especially because of his popularity with fans and the key role he plays in the team's offense. So, what's the status of Kmet's injury, and will he be back this season? Here's the latest Cole Kmet injury update. Bears coach Ben Johnson shares an update on Cole Kmet's knee injury after Thursday night's win Bears head coach Ben Johnson was honest about Kmet's condition after the game. He was asked about it, of course, during the postgame presser and said the team was planning a deeper evaluation on Monday to find out just how serious Kmet's right knee injury is right now. He also said , "I don't think it looked very good." The Bears haven't hinted at how long Kmet will be out due to his knee injury. Since Johnson admitted that it didn't look good, though, that's a sign that he could be out for a while. The team will conduct testing and have medical experts determine the severity of the injury and how much time he'll miss. When Kmet is sidelined, Colston Loveland will get time on the field, as will third-round rookie Sam Roush. The extra playing time will be helpful for developing Roush, so that's a silver lining in this situation. item.title: Arsenal boss Slegers taking it game-by-game after difficult run
item.description: Arsenal boss Slegers taking it game-by-game after difficult run Arsenal head coach Renée Slegers says that she is taking things game-by-game after a difficult start to the season. The Gunners have won just one of their six Barclays Women’s Super League matches and currently occupy eighth place in the table. Arsenal are already 12 points behind leaders Manchester City. When speaking to the media ahead of this weekend’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture at Tottenham Hotspur, Slegers said that she is taking things game-by-game rather than looking at the standings. “At the moment, I’m not looking at the table – my mindset is to take it game-by-game,” Slegers said. “The next one is the North London derby, we look forward to it coming right now. The fight we will bring for the fans tomorrow is the only thing we’re thinking about.” There has been discontent coming from the stands in recent games. Slegers understands the Arsenal fans’ frustration and says that the team want to grab the North London bragging rights for them. She said “I can’t be thinking about that [noise from the crowd]. Looking back, that was the sound of care, I think, what we heard at the stadium. So many people in the stadium buying a ticket to watch us play and that was the sound of care and the sound of frustration, which was totally to its right. “Tomorrow, we are blessed with the fans that we have and that they’re showing up and that we’re selling out the away section. We’re going to do it for them because I know how much they want it and I know how much they’re invested and that’s going to be a big thing for us.” Some have questioned whether a change in management is needed at Arsenal, but Slegers is not focusing on past results or external opinions, she is looking towards the next game. She said “That’s not something I think about. It’s about where we are as a group and what we’re working towards. It’s absolutely not what we wanted or expected eight games into the season, but I’m in the here-and-now. “We’re preparing for the North London derby tomorrow and we have the group together in the same direction. The fuel and motivation is sky-high because of the fans that will be there for us, that’s where my focus is.” Arsenal’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture at Tottenham Hotspur kicks-off at 12.45pm on Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Dad says Guilderland's coed bowling team sidelines girls in competitions
item.description: Meghan Anderson wants to play on a girls bowling team at Guilderland High School. The student, who is in seventh grade now, could play on the school's coed team. That team lets girls practice -but only the top players can compete, which, her father says, is usually the boys. (Provided by Darren Anderson) GUILDERLAND - A local parent is invoking a landmark civil rights law to add a girls' bowling team at Guilderland High School. The school has a coed team now. And unlike tackle sports, it's the sort of activity that could be played by mixed-gender groups. But in reality, the boys dominate because they have much stronger arm strength, parent Darren Anderson said. He told the Guilderland school board earlier this week that under Title XI, the 1972 legislation that requires equitable treatment for male and female athletes, they should offer a girls' team. Title XI banned sex discrimination at schools that receive federal funding. It opened the door to sports for many women. "At the college level, Title IX has helped women's bowling become an official, fully sanctioned NCAA championship sport," he said. While anyone can join Guilderland's coed team, only the top few players can compete in matches. Usually, that's all boys, he said. "Of course, boys are stronger, but really there's physics to it," he said. "Girls actually have to be more accurate than boys because they don't have as much power." A boy who hits the pins slightly off-center can hit them with enough power to knock over the pins, while the girl with less power must hit the pins just right. And if a girl is competing with a boy who has both power and aim, she's often outmatched, he said. "So they don't start. You don't really have a chance to play the matches," Anderson said. "They practice, but they don't compete, because you have to have one of the six top averages to do that." In the 13-school Suburban Council, there are nine high schools with girls' bowling teams. At Guilderland, there are 15 girls interested in joining a girls team, he said. Anderson's daughter Meghan is in seventh grade. She's not trying to become an elite bowler. But she likes the sport, which she says has value as a lifelong physical activity. "Bowling is a sport you can do for a very long time," she said. Her favorite part isn't the bowling. "You get to socialize and meet new people," she said. She competes against boys at a junior league now, using a point system in which players get a handicap if their average score is much higher than their opponent's average. In high school matches, there are no handicaps. "I think that we should have a girls' bowling team because it would be more fair," she said. item.title: Breaking: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany taken to hospital after collapse
item.description: (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images Concern is growing around Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany after Bild reported that the Belgian manager was taken to a hospital in Munich by ambulance on Friday. According to the report, a helicopter had landed earlier at Bayern’s training ground on Säbener Straße. Further details about the circumstances surrounding the incident have not yet been confirmed. This is the exact wording posted by @iMiaSanMia ): ❕ Vincent Kompany was taken to a Munich hospital by ambulance today. A helicopter had landed at the training ground on Säbener Straße earlier. More info shortly. Sky Germany (via @ iMiaSanMia ) is reporting that Kompany collapsed at training; Vincent Kompany collapsed after today’s training session. The coach was immediately taken to a hospital by ambulance. A rescue helicopter had landed at the training ground earlier. Kompany had been battling a severe illness (reported to be a viral infection) and a hip issue ahead of Bayern Munich’s Champions League game against Arsenal, but he was cleared to return to the bench. Bayern Munich is now preparing for Sunday’s Bundesliga clash against SC Freiburg following Wednesday’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League. The most important thing is Kompany’s health and well-being. Understandably, Bayern Munich supporters are hoping that the situation is not serious and that the 40-year-old coach is receiving the care he needs. item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 17: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) greets fans as he walks into the stadium ahead of the game between the Texas Longhorns and Florida Gators, Oct. 17, 2026. (Sara Diggins/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images) The No. 19 Texas Longhorns continue their precipitous fall from grace through the first three games of conference play. An embarrassing loss to the Oklahoma Sooners spun into another embarrassing loss at home to the Florida Gators, a pair of unranked teams that Texas should have taken care of handily. Now, the road gets tougher and Texas has yet to show signs of life. The toughest stretch of SEC play for the Longhorns kicks off Saturday with a visit from the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels and one of the most dynamic players in the country. New head coach Pete Golding won the offseason early by keeping quarterback Trinidad Chambliss in Oxford, who paces an offense led by an elite running back in Kewan Lacy and a group of talented pass catchers. Chambliss has been everything Texas fans hoped Arch Manning would be: catalytic in the passing game, elusive with his feet, and ultimately a winner in big spots. When it was winning time against former head coach Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers, Chambliss was at his best. When they faced off against outmatched opponents, he and the offense bullied them all over the field. item.title: ‘I try not to think about it’: Harry Kane opens up on Ballon d’Or stress as England striker eyes historic award
item.description: ‘I try not to think about it’: Harry Kane opens up on Ballon d’Or stress as England striker eyes historic award Harry Kane has admitted that waiting to find out whether he will win the Ballon d’Or is stressful, and the England captain said he has no idea what to expect ahead of Monday’s ceremony in London. The Bayern Munich striker is one of the favourites to win football’s most prestigious individual award after an outstanding season in which he scored 61 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions. Kane helped Bayern win the domestic double and reach the Champions League semi-final last season, where they were beaten by eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain. Winning the Ballon d’Or would make the 33-year-old the first English player to receive the award since Michael Owen in 2001. But he faces competition from Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe. Yamal had an impressive campaign. He helped Barcelona win La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup, and also played a key role in Spain’s World Cup triumph in the United States. The teenager recorded 48 goal contributions in 58 appearances across all competitions. Despite being the bookmakers’ favourite, Kane says he hasn’t been told whether he will win the award at the London Palladium. Speaking about the uncertainty, the striker admitted that he would prefer to know the result beforehand rather than wait through the entire ceremony. “They want everyone to go, all the big names there, and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know, so I can understand why,” he said (via the Daily Mail ). “From my point of view, of course, I’d love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. “But it is their decision, I can’t control that. We’ll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much. “I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rumours flying around, and you try to stay away from it. “Of course I am going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It is a big occasion so we will have to wait and see.” Kane, who recently agreed a new contract with Bayern , was in fine form for the Bundesliga holders in the Champions League. He notched a goal and an assist in the 2-2 draw against Arsenal. He has also scored 10 goals and provided seven assists in 11 games across all competitions this season.

item.title: Boost for Carrick as he confirms versatile Man Utd star is ‘back with the group’ for Bournemouth clash
item.description: Boost for Carrick as he confirms versatile Man Utd star is ‘back with the group’ for Bournemouth clash Michael Carrick has confirmed that Ayden Heaven is ‘back with the group’ after missing the last two matches through illness. It seems as though he is currently Manchester United’s only returnee for Sunday’s clash with Bournemouth, although Carrick did suggest other players could also make the squad depending on how they recover today and tomorrow. United team news: Who’s missing? (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) His other absentees include Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford, Patrick Dorgu, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte. Martinez sustained a thigh problem in the first half of last Sunday’s draw with Leeds United, while Rashford is said to have been carrying a hip injury since the World Cup . There are concerns over Sesko’s condition, as he has not featured since before the September international break due to a re-aggravation of a previous issue. United chiefs are reportedly undecided on whether the Slovenian will need surgery to correct the injury once and for all, which could see him sidelined for a more lengthy period. Bournemouth welcome injury boost before Old Trafford trip Meanwhile, Bournemouth have been granted a major boost in the form of attacking starlet Eli Junior Kroupi being fit. He has been out of action since July, but returned to full first-team training this week, and is in line to play at Old Trafford. “It’s the plan to take him with us to Manchester, and to give him some minutes,” manager Marco Rose said of Kroupi in his pre-United press conference. “He is a funny guy. I love him. He has a good attitude, and he is a special player. We have to take care of him, and he needs to take care of his next steps.” https://twitter.com/brfootball/status/2056822880810197159?s=61 The Cherries are fresh off the back of an unforgettable victory after they overturned AC Milan 3-0 in a Europa League tie at the Vitality Stadium on Thursday night, so they’ll be looking to use that momentum to really crack on and turn things around in the Premier League. item.title: Spalletti wants more from Kolo Muani and Woltemade when they start together
item.description: Spalletti wants more from Kolo Muani and Woltemade when they start together Juventus finally started Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade together after the pair had impressed when playing alongside each other in the second half of several matches in the past. Their performances in those appearances had encouraged hopes that they could develop a strong partnership and provide the team with another reliable source of goals. The opportunity came against Rennes last night, but the Old Lady could not secure a victory, settling for a 2-2 draw . Woltemade scored from the penalty spot, although neither forward managed to find the net from open play as Juventus struggled to get the goals they needed. The result means there is still work to do before the partnership delivers the attacking impact that supporters are hoping to see. Juventus will have further opportunities to start the two forwards together, giving them more time to understand each other’s movement and develop a stronger connection in the final third. Juventus seek a stronger attacking partnership Many fans have believed that Juventus would score more regularly whenever both players were on the pitch together . Their previous performances had created expectations that the combination could offer the team greater attacking threat, so the failure to see either player score from open play against Rennes was likely to disappoint those supporters. However, one match is not enough to determine whether the partnership can fulfil its potential. The two forwards will need time and further opportunities to demonstrate how effectively they can complement each other, particularly when Juventus are looking for goals against difficult opposition. The club are expected to continue trusting both players individually, while the coaching staff remain hopeful that their combined qualities can produce better results. There is still confidence that the partnership can work, but the latest performance has shown that improvement is needed. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Spalletti expects more from both forwards Luciano Spalletti has acknowledged that he wants more from the pair when they play together. Although the Juventus manager was satisfied with aspects of their performance, he believes their individual abilities should allow them to contribute more in attack. The manager had expected a goal from the partnership, and he made his assessment clear at the end of the game, as quoted by Tuttojuve : “We’ve already done that. They played well today, but I think I can expect more from both of them because their qualities are superior to their performance tonight. They played a good game today, but they can do more.” Spalletti’s comments suggest that Juventus will continue working with both forwards while expecting a greater return from their attacking partnership in future matches.

item.title: NY Giants have sprung some leaks on special teams the past 2 weeks
item.description: Charlie Jones | Getty Images Through the first four games of the season, the New York Giants special teams were rock solid. That has not been the case the past two weeks as the Giants have tied the Washington Commanders and lost to the New Orleans Saints. Sunday in the loss to the Saints, there were a number of special teams errors: Charlie Jones fumbled a kickoff return with less two minutes remaining in the first half, setting up the Saints in position to tie the game before halftime. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. I’m a very simple person. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn.
